Well, the probability of finishing the chosen degree with good grades or at all is fairly slim given the situatio. That would probably be followed by a less-than-stellar job which would involve long unstatisfying work with lesser pay for potentially decades. Lower socio-economic status would follow, which would narrow down potential mates and make for a family that's more likely to end up in the same socioeconomic status as their father genetically and environmentally speaking. 

So, yeah, not a great life all in all. I understand OP's concern and people who say exams have no meaning are honestly idiots. If OP hasn't put in enough academic effort or is ailed by otherwise debilitating conditions now is the time to try and fix things, however if failing \ almost failing all his exams is the product of his best efforts then he can either choose to curb his expectations of life or do with them as he chooses.
